snippet.title: Why Saudi Arabia Will Never Let Oil Hit $200
snippet.description:
*The Real Reason Saudi Arabia Will Always Side With America*

Eleven men sit around a table deciding the price of oil for the entire world. Ten of them want to raise it. One walks out, flies home to talk to his king, comes back eight hours later, and quietly torpedoes the whole thing.

*That moment is why the Middle East looks the way it does today.*

This isn't really a story about diplomacy or alliances. It's a story about the math underneath all of it — what it actually costs Saudi Arabia to pull a barrel of oil out of the ground (*$3*), what Iran needed to sell it for to keep their economy from collapsing (*$19*), and the one thing that genuinely terrifies a petrostate: not low prices, but prices so high the world finds a replacement and stops needing you at all.

*In this one we get into:*

— Why the *Ghawar oil field* is basically cheating, and how Saudi Arabia gets 10,000 barrels out of a well using the same electricity it takes Texas to get 500

— What a *"fiscal breakeven" price* actually is, and why $40 oil is fine for some countries and a death sentence for others

— How the *Stevenson Plan* killed the British rubber monopoly in the 1920s, and why every Saudi oil minister since has been quietly haunted by it

— Why Saudi Arabia did to *American shale in 2016* what they did to *Iran in 1976* — and what that reveals about who the kingdom is actually loyal to

*The short version:* Saudi Arabia doesn't pick friends. It picks self-interest. Sometimes that lines up with America. Sometimes it doesn't. The oil math explains all of it.

snippet.title: The Single Force Driving Today’s Global Conflicts
snippet.description:
China / Taiwan. Russia / Ukraine. USA / Iran. 

Why is the world erupting into war right now? There are a few reasons - economic, ideological, historical. 

But the main reason that many people overlook is something much more fundamental. They're all actually about controlling geographic chokepoints. 

A geographic chokepoint is a point on the map where a lot of important movement gets squeezed through. Food, oil, ships, armies. Because of this, their blockade would have the potential to cripple the economies of certain countries, and have ramifications around the world. 

This video explores the geographic chokepoints driving the conflict in Ukraine and the upcoming conflict in Taiwan. We'll look at the Taiwan Strait and how it's a crucial trade lane for Japan and South Korea. We'll look at the Black Sea, and the key sea ports of Odesa and Sevastopol. We'll also look at the land chokepoints and Russia's history of being invaded - going back to Nazi Germany and Napoleon. 

We'll understand why Putin, Xi and Trump are so keen to plunge their nations into war - controlling these points is that important!

localized.title: Why Our Economy STILL Doesn't Run On Renewable Energy
localized.description:
With all the chaos around oil in Iran and Strait of Hormuz, why don't we just switch to renewable energy sources? Why doesn't our economy run on solar power, wind power, hydro, geothermal, or nuclear? Oil seems like an outdated system, and for decades politicians have been promising a green revolution. So where is it?

Download our FREE Financial Jargon Cheat Sheet here: https://lockstockfinance.eo.page/2d5hf

In this video, we'll explain why our economy hasn't switched over to renewables energy sources. It's not as easy as 'just stopping oil'. The energy infrastructure of our modern economy is firmly embedded. And despite major advances in renewable technology - solar, wind, nuclear, geothermal and hydro - we don't quite have the technology to meet the energy demands of the complex electricity grid. Battery technology has come a long way, but it will be a while yet before we can truly stop oil.

snippet.title: Can AI Predict a Football Match?
snippet.description:
Can AI predict a football / soccer match in real time?

⚽️ DeepMind's TacticAI treats all 22 players as a connected network, not just dots on a map.
🎯 Trained on 7,000+ Premier League corners, it predicts who touches the ball first and whether it leads to a shot.
🤯 Liverpool's own experts couldn't tell its generated setups from real ones (and preferred its calls 90% of the time)
🔮 It's now moving into open play with Palmeiras, simulating the ripple effect of a single tactical change
